summary.intent: Debug email OTP login failure in the macOS desktop release build, then add and plan Phase 41 (package/app versioning and release cycles) including a deep discussion of the versioning strategy.
summary.outcome: OTP bug root-caused and fixed (split-brain API URL between JS compile-time env and Rust runtime env, plus error masking) with PR #425 created; Phase 41 added to roadmap and fully contextualized with decisions on release signal source, version grouping, staging flow, and CI enforcement.

repo: The Tauri desktop app has a split configuration: JS reads VITE_API_URL at Vite compile time, while Rust reads it at runtime via std::env::var(), falling back to localhost:3000 in release builds.
Tauri invoke() rejections are plain strings, not Error objects — instanceof Error checks silently swallow the real error message.
release-please-config.json is the authoritative source for package path → component name mapping and can be reused as input to CI label enforcement.
The API, TS api-client, and Rust api-client are tightly coupled via the OpenAPI spec (openapi.json); clients are generated from the spec and should be versioned as a locked group.
Staging deploys are triggered by staging-v* tags and are fully independent from the main release flow; deploy-staging.yml has separate jobs per component already structured for conditional skipping.
All four build targets (web, macOS, Windows, Linux) in deploy-staging.yml set VITE_API_URL, so option_env!("VITE_API_URL") in Rust will pick it up at compile time during CI.
The project uses squash-merge strategy, which collapses individual conventional commits — this is the root cause of Release Please's inability to do per-package bump granularity.
Individual PR commits are accessible via GitHub API before squash and contain both conventional type and file-change information sufficient to auto-compute per-package bump intent.

code.finding: Rust reads API URL from runtime env var with localhost:3000 fallback — fixed by adding option_env!("VITE_API_URL") as compile-time fallback before localhost.
OTP verify catch block uses `err instanceof Error` which is false for Tauri invoke rejections (plain strings), causing real error to be swallowed and generic 'Verification failed' shown.
Same instanceof Error masking pattern exists in the MFA recovery catch block — fixed in the same PR.
VITE_API_URL set for Vite build step but the same env var is available to the Tauri action's cargo build, so option_env! will resolve it at Rust compile time.

workflow: The GSD debug workflow spawns isolated subagents to protect main context window from file-reading/hypothesis overhead.
The discuss-phase workflow supports an 'assumptions' mode where the agent analyzes the codebase first and presents beliefs for correction rather than asking open-ended questions.

release-as per-package directive in release-please-config.json can be used as a one-shot override to force exact version targets, bypassing RP's commit analysis — consumed and cleared when RP creates the release PR.

PR commit list (pre-squash) is accessible via GitHub API and can be parsed for conventional commit type + file paths to auto-compute per-package bump intent before the squash destroys per-commit granularity.

friction: The split-brain API URL issue was silent — the JS side succeeded, the Rust side silently failed with a connection error that was swallowed by the instanceof Error check, producing only a generic 'Verification failed' message with no actionable detail.
Release Please's path-based bump detection combined with squash merges creates imprecise per-package versioning — a long design session was needed to arrive at a workable solution.
The discuss-phase workflow required reading the same large workflow file multiple times due to its length.
The 'enrich RP' vs 'replace with Changesets' vs 'release-as injection' decision path required significant back-and-forth before arriving at the PR commit analysis approach.
open_items: Phase 41 planning not yet started — CONTEXT.md written, next step is /gsd:plan-phase 41.
PR #425 (OTP fix) needs a new staging build (new staging-v* tag) to validate the fix in a release binary — user has not yet tested a locally built instance.
PR-time GitHub Action to auto-analyze PR commits, compute per-package bump labels, and detect cascades needs to be designed and implemented.
Post-merge GitHub Action to read final labels and write release-as directives to release-please-config.json needs to be implemented.
Label vocabulary (~70 labels: release:component:feat/fix/perf/refactor/breaking + release:none) needs to be pre-created in the GitHub repo.
Cascade detection script (~100-150 lines) using pnpm list --json and cargo metadata to auto-add dependent package labels at PR time.
Staging tag format change from staging-v{semver} to staging-{date}-release-{n} (e.g. staging-20260331-release-1) needs to be implemented.
Docker image dual-tagging strategy (component version tag + latest-staging rolling tag) needs to be wired into deploy-staging.yml.
Decision on whether to add path-based change detection to staging workflow to skip unchanged components — deferred as a Phase 2 optimization.
Web and desktop versioning strategy (monotonic v1, v2, v3) needs to be reflected in release-please-config.json — currently both likely use semver.
Root package milestone-marker bumping process needs to be defined (currently bumped manually, but process is informal).
